work.title: Musik til Adam Oehlenschlägers dramatiske eventyr "Fiskeren og hans Børn"
Music for Adam Oehlenschläger's Dramatic Fairy Tale "The Fisherman and his Children"

history.p: Oehlenschläger's dramatic fairy tale was originally a poem, which he arranged for the theatre. The play was intended for performance on the occasion of the silver wedding of the new King Christian VIII and Queen Caroline Amalie. In November 1839, Oehlenschläger informed the director of The Royal Theatre, that Hartmann had promised to write the music; a month later, however, the poet changed his mind. In order to save time, he wanted already existing music from two of Weyse's operas but dropped this plan again. Therefore Hartmann did not get the text until two months before the premiere. His music was highly praised by the critics, whereas Oehlenschläger's play was very badly received. After three performances it was removed from the repertoire for ever.

physDesc.physMedium: Bound in brown leather with marbled sides. Handwritten label pasted on front cover, inscribed: "Fiskeren og hans Børn / Partitur." Stamped: "Det Kongelige Theaters Eiendom." Written in brown ink. Paper: 12, 16 and 18 staves. Many different paginations in upper right-hand corners. Later pagination in pencil at bottom of each page 1-151 (p. 118 omitted by mistake), 2 last pages blank. Above No. 1 in upper right-hand corner Hartmann has later written "til Dante" in purple ink, referring to Chr. K.F. Molbech's play (HartW 23). Pages 111-112 is a violin part with the heading: "Dands af 'Ravnen' Indlagt Til Partituret." Referring to "Ravnen" (HartW 1). Pages 136-137 is a loose folio in different format written in purple ink with the heading "No 4, Forspil til 5te Akt Dante", p. 137 blank. No. 12 has been cancelled in pencil. At the end of the music on p. 151, signed and dated: "I:P:E: Hartmann Op: 28. / Mai 1840."
